steps.name: Swire
steps.text: So this is the Rhodes Island Siesta branch office?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: How did you know—

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I happen to have a few friends at Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: You're a tour guide, aren't you? Don't tell me you're giving tours of a pharmaceutical company now.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I, I was driving a guest...

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Save me the excuses.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: It's dangerous for an Oripathy patient to hide his identity, regardless of reason. It's against the law, even in Siesta.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Yes, I know!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: But what am I supposed to...?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Then you work so many jobs—and swindled me—because of Oripathy?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: ...and family.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: What happens to me doesn't matter, but I worry about what happens to them when I'm gone.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I just need time... until the shop moves and we have a new future...

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Don't look at me like that. I'm not asking for your sympathy.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: No, I just remembered how much you charged me the other day compared to the average taxi price here.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Well, you lied about being a normal tourist...

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Oh? You've got a sharper tongue than one would think.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: What do you want?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Let's make a deal.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: You saw that chap from MountainDash Logistics the other day, in the bar. He's my competitor.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: We're competing for the rebuilding rights in the commercial district, but he has home-ground advantage. I need some local help to even the odds.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: You work for me, and I never saw you today. How's that?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: You're trying to blackmail—

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Now, now, there's no need for such language. You scratch my back, I scratch yours. And don't worry, you'll be paid.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I don't need a handout...

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: And I'm not giving any handouts. All I want is a fair deal.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: What's your deal?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I run a clean business here. We don't do forced relocations and the like. If everybody wins, so much the better.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Now, there's always going to be controversy when it comes to rebuilding. But I promise that I'll do better than MountainDash Logistics.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: We've already worked together once, after all. May I count on your vote?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I just want my family's bar to be relocated smoothly...

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Deal, then.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Oh, and one little word of advice.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: No matter what you have to deal with, Oripathy treatment is not something that can be delayed. You should make up your mind soon.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Aren't you concerned about dealing with an Infected?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I have a friend who's Infected too.
It is almost closing time at the museum. There are no tourists, but the audio tours continue to play on loop. The massive mountain boulder remains silent in the empty gallery.

a.text: 'The Naumanns left behind thousands of photos and samples...'
'The rebuilding of the villages around Mount Unna...'
'They visited more than a hundred volcanos across numerous countries...'

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: Did you really see it?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Yes! I saw the ice cream come in here!

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: You just wanted to come to the museum.

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: I knew we wouldn't find it. He was lying to us. He didn't go to all those places...

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: How did you get in? Admission is closed.

steps.name: Frightened Boy
steps.text: Sorry... we'll be going.

steps.name: Innocent Girl
steps.text: Have you seen my dad?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Your dad?

steps.name: Innocent Girl
steps.text: We're looking for a... er... er... adventurer?

steps.name: Innocent Girl
steps.text: He went to a lot of places! In the photos he sent us, there were volcanoes, snow mountains, hills in nomadic cities...

steps.name: Innocent Girl
steps.text: His photo might be in the Volcano Museum!

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: What's your father's name?

steps.name: Innocent Girl
steps.text: Chuck!

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: I've never heard of a volcanologist by that name. Maybe you should ask elsewhere.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I may know your dad.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: What are you doing here, Adele? And you look awful...

steps.name: Innocent Girl
steps.text: You've seen him?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: You said your dad was an adventurer?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Where has he been?

steps.name: Innocent Girl
steps.text: I don't know... he always sends back photos when he visits a place.

steps.name: Innocent Girl
steps.text: I think the last one was from Sargon.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Sargon! I knew it.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: My parents were volcanic researchers. They told me a story about when they were surveying in Sargon...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: They quickly lost their way in the thick branches and leaves of the rainforest, and it felt like they were wandering around the stomach of a great beast.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Just as they thought they would never get out, they saw a man with leaves all over him.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: 'Are you lost? Do you need any help?'

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: He pointed the way for them and took them out of the rainforest. They even saw a sight of sunny rain. My parents were really thankful.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: 'Thank you so much for helping us out of there! What is your name, sir?'

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: The man brushed off the leaves, took a photo of the rainforest, and said, 'No need to thank me. The name's Chuck. I'm taking this photo to send to my kids.'

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: And that's how the photo made it to you.

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: Really? Sounds made-up...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Of course it's true!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I think I have a photo here somewhere...
Adele digs through the papers and takes out a photo of the Naumanns smiling at the camera, with a few blurred figures behind them.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Look, here's your dad.

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: (I'm still not sure that's actually my dad...)

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: (I can't see him clearly, but...)

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: (I hope he's my dad! That means he helped other adventurers find their way and sent us a photo! What a cool dad!)

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: (I didn't know you were a storyteller.)

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: (Just repeating something I heard from mom when I was little, with a few adjustments here and there.)

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: (There's no reason for a professional volcanic survey team to accept help from an amateur. The story sounds entirely unscientific.)

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: (Science exists to bring hope to people, doesn't it?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Well, we can't have them running around the museum like this. If their parent or guardian isn't here, I'll take them home.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: You look tired, Adele. You should get some rest too.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Come, kids, I'll take you home.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Kahn, I think I should do it.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: But you...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: It's fine. Let me do it.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: They look lonely... I'll keep them company.

steps.name: Excited Boy
steps.text: Enis!

steps.name: Excited Girl
steps.text: Enis!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Where did you go?

steps.name: Joyful Girl
steps.text: I found out where dad went!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Make sure you tell your family the next time you go out.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: It's you...?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Huh? You're...

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I'm the one who ran into you today and knocked you out... I'm Enis. I'm their brother. Are you okay? Any dizziness? Dr. Ceylon said... er, she said...

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I'm sorry! I didn't mean to run off, but I had to go to work. I'll pay your medical expenses—

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Dr. Ceylon told me everything. It's not your fault.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Your little brother and sister must be hungry. You should go home.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Er...

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Thank you so much... what's your name?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Call me Adele.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I'll remember... little ones, don't you have something to say to Adele?

steps.name: Girl & Boy
steps.text: Thank you, Adele!
The mischievous boy reaches around the little girl's neck and pats her opposite shoulder.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Huh? Who's there?
The girl looks hesitantly at the troublemaker next to her, who pretends nothing has happened, but could not hold back his laughter.
They chase each other into the shop, into the open arms of their mother, then run back out like frolicking beastling, while their mother tends to dinner being cooked on the stovetop.
Adele breaks out in a smile.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: That's so nice to see.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mr. Enis, do you know one Mr. Pelipper?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: The Volcano Museum needs obsidian for its research. I heard you may be able to acquire some...

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Damn, he just can't keep his mouth shut, can he...?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Could I buy some from you?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: You helped me so much, I should repay the favor.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I dug these up around the volcano three months ago. They don't look great, but maybe they'll be useful for your research.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Thank you very much!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: However, I must ask you to stay away from the volcano. If you know anyone else who is mining for obsidian, please also tell them to stop doing so.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mount Siesta has entered its active period. Even if it hasn't erupted yet, Originium activity in the area continues to increase.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: There is a risk of Oripathy infection without professional protective equipment.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Well, I...
There is laughter coming in from outside, as the two children chase each other on the streets, as their shadows stretch in the setting sun.
Enis gazes at his siblings as they go further and further away, and subconsciously touches the spot on his chest where he was scratched by Originium.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Alright, I promise I won't go anymore.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: And thank you for playing with my siblings. That should have been my responsibility as big brother.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: It's okay. They're very cute. I had a good time too.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: By the way, your siblings said that your father has not been home for a long time?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: He's a, er, adventurer? Traveler? Explorer?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: It's not like he's gone off the grid or anything. He sends postcards and money back on a regular basis.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: You can be present without actually being there. However...

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: By the time we get a letter from him, he's already off to the next place. All we know is that there's someone out there, going from one corner of the land to the other.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Sometimes I want to see for myself where he's been.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Harley raised us here while running the shop. But she says that life is a journey, and everyone chooses the sights they want to see.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: If you don't mind me asking... why are the three of you all different races?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Well, we're not blood-related...

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: All three of us were adopted.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: No need to look at me like that. It's not exactly taboo.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: People come and go every year, some seeking a new life, some seeking romance.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Many leave in disappointment when they find that life here isn't all it's cracked up to be, leaving behind children like us.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I can tell your siblings love you.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: It must seem strange to outsiders, but for me, family is family. Ties of blood aren't that important.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I don't know what my birth parents looked like. Maybe they abandoned me, or maybe they loved me, and got into an accident.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: My new parents didn't hide anything from me. The little ones will be told the truth too, once they're a little older.
Adele looks at Harley, working in the shop, and Enis's siblings, who are already shadows in the distance. Everything is warm and peaceful, like a dream.
The obsidian feels heavy. She turns sideways and wipes away a teardrop from the corner of her eye.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: And how long were you planning to hide it from me, Enis?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: —Mom?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Alright, I admit, I have thought of remaking this place into a hot springs resort...

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I promise I won't try to do it behind your back! I won't do anything without your permission—

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Once you've gotten everything in order, once arrangements for our future have been made the way you wanted.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Then you'll leave your mother and siblings behind the way you clear a drunkard out of the bar, and find a place to wait for Oripathy to take you?

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Is that the journey you've chosen for yourself?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: ...You knew?

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: I was waiting for you to tell me.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mr. Enis, you're already—

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Well, blame me and my fat fingers... I got scratched by Originium when I was digging for obsidian at the volcano.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I thought I was good at climbing...

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Yeah, I learned my lesson...

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: No, the only thing you learned to is to hide things from me, and you're not half as good as you think you are at it.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: You've got that look on your face that says 'I'm gonna finish everything, go far away, and tell my blissfully ignorant mother everything in a farewell letter after I die.' You think it's cool.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Now you've got that look on your face that says 'I can't even say that's not what's going on'.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I-I didn't think it was cool. I just felt like it's what I have to do as a big brother... as a part of this family.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: After all, w-we're not...

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Even if you didn't do anything, you'll still be their brother, and my son. There is no bargaining in love.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: If you insist on bargaining with me about this, young man, let me tell you that you'll be working off your debt for a long time.

spans.text: If you insist on bargaining with me about this, young man, let me tell you that you'll be working off your debt for a

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Oh, sorry, I thought some background music was in order for a scene like this.

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Name's Byrd. Traveling troubadour.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Our resident singer now.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: You can afford a resident singer?

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: No, but this one only wants to be paid a story.

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Your Kazimierz story was wonderful. It helped a great deal in understanding the folk tunes of those parts.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Can I borrow your guitar?

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Let me play a song.
The evening mist covers the town ♪
The rising new moon makes it look like a new place ♪
My favorite place exists only in my sweet memories ♪
I have nothing but my sweet memories ♪

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: So you came here.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: How far can you see from here?

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: It's all dark... just empty seas.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Not being able to see means you can imagine!

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: There's actually an island on the far side of the sea, and everyone who leaves Siesta lives on the island.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: I'm a little scared... when we grow up, will our parents and Enis leave us...

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: He won't!

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: Enis says we're an adventure team!

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: A team doesn't leave each other. We'll go back to Old Siesta, and many other places...

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: You can't tell there's something on Enis's mind?

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: What? How do you have something on a mind?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: You're an idiot.
The girl stands up, gazes at the direction of the volcano, and yells with all her strength.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Hey—Old Siesta—

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: I miss you—

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Will you stop being angry?

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: It's a loss for the Obsidian Festival that your performance was not part of it.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: There's nothing to be lost. Siesta has heard my music many times. I don't need to compete for attention with young people at a music festival.

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: You're a Siestan with rock n' roll spirit.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: In my case, I added the Siestan identity to a rock n' roll spirit.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Chuck and I met on our travels in Siesta.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: We heard about the wondrous sight of the 'White Volcano,' how the entire volcano turns white like a marshmallow under certain weather conditions.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: We spent a year in Siesta without seeing a sight of it, but we fell in love with the city and settled down here, opening a little shop.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: If we couldn't find the 'White Volcano,' we could make one ourselves.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: So that's how the shop got its name? I thought you two just came up with it on the fly.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Dr. Keller has talked about the legend of the White Volcano before... but does it really exist?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Might be snow if it's just the top of the mountain, but when you're talking about the whole mountain... I don't know of any phenomenon like that.

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Whether it actually exists or not is not important. The scene of legends has taken root in new soil, even creating a new legend of its own—

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: What a beautiful story.

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: This reminds me of an old song that was written in Siesta.

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: May I?
It's a long, long journey ♪
I write on a ship with a broken mast ♪
My home is a hundred miles behind me ♪
How charming is the summer sun ♪
The North Wind blows a hundred miles, visiting the first volcano ♪
We'll meet again, along the forgotten trail ♪

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Oh! I remember now! This is it!

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: 'The North Wind blows a hundred miles, visiting the first volcano ♪'!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: That's the North Wind you're looking for?

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Having a tune play itself over and over in your head but not being able to remember the lyrics is the seventh most painful thing in the world.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: I'm feeling much better now! Thanks!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Adele? Who are you talking to?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Er... myself!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Just thinking about the 'North Wind' in the lyrics.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: But Siesta is north of the ocean. It should be the south wind in the summer...

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: I'm reminded of a story about the songwriter. I think it was back in 1060?

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: His album, 'Lost,' tells the story of how he got lost in the hills on a camping trip and had to be rescued.

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: The album was a smash hit, and cemented how the singer 'couldn't find the north.'

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Maybe he got his directions mixed up.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Is that all there is to it?

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: The events of the past can often feel like a joke. We just seeing a snapshot preserved in time, but the actual truth is elusive.

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: That's why the present is so precious, isn't it?

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Ain't that right.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: What are you doing, Enis?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: P-Putting the sign up.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Ha! You stubborn boy.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: A hand...? Mom.
Enis stands on the ladder, lifting up the shop sign.
He takes the hammer and nail from his mother, and goes to work pinning it above the door.
The power switch is pulled, and neon-illuminated words begin to glow against the sun's last light.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: White... Volcano?

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: The original Messenger for this batch called in sick. The letter was already like that when I got it. This was the only place I could think of when I saw 'volcano' on the envelope.

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: I know as much as you do, if there's no information about the sender on the letter, there's no information.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: 'How have you been? I'm doing fine here.'

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: 'It's been a long time. I miss you.'

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: 'The volcano is a spectacular sight. The winds are strong at the peak.'

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: 'Love, Your Father'

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mr. Enis... might this photo be from your father?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: My father?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: This is... Mount Unna! He really did go there!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Mom! Dad sent a photo! Want to see?

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Write back to him and tell him that he loses his bet if he sends another postcard photo and not one that he actually took himself.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: After all, I raised my son to be cool, while all he does is steal other people's photos.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Real adventurers don't do that.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: I'll bring these obsidian samples back. We should have a more accurate estimate of the eruption time.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Glad to be of help.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: ...Adele, do you know why Keller called you to Siesta?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Some of the exhibits in the Volcano Museum were connected to my parents' research. Dr. Keller asked me to help organize things.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I'm not sure I understand your concerns...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: In their last days, my parents were studying the relationship between Originium veins and volcanic activity. There are many other people doing the same. Why would there be danger?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: I wasn't sure it was my place to tell you what Dr. Naumann tried to hide from you... but hide this any longer, and you may never have the chance to learn the truth.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: In the year before Dr. Naumann died, her lab was frequently contacted by the personal army of a Leithanian Kurfürst.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Army...?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: The Naumanns were experts in Originium and ecology. Their research converged on the prediction and prevention of Catastrophes.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: But someone may have seen another possibility in their research.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Weaponization...

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: I was studying abroad at the time, so what I knew was limited to rumors in my classmates' messages.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: There was only one person who had access to their research.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Keller.
